title: Learned five-gene panel discriminates Alzheimer’s tissue samples in retrospective datasets
summary: LASSO, support-vector recursive feature elimination and random forests selected five Alzheimer’s-associated genes after expression, co-expression and disease-pathway screening. A five-gene nomogram had reported AUCs of 0.907 in a 195-sample dataset and 0.776 in a separate 100-sample dataset; PLCB1 also correlated with pathology-stage and neuronal measures. These retrospective tissue associations do not establish a clinical diagnostic workflow, a causal disease mechanism or effective treatment. The selected genes were screened within an already annotated Alzheimer’s pathway; no first identification of these genes or experimental validation of proposed drugs is claimed.
ai_technology: LASSO; SVM-RFE; random forest; gene-expression nomogram
organization: Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University; Guangdong Medical University

evidence.tested: Training expression dataset: 97 Alzheimer’s/98 control samples. Separate dataset: 56 Alzheimer’s/44 control samples. Five-gene nomogram AUC 0.907/0.776; additional stage and single-cell analyses provided biological context.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective tissue datasets, not clinical diagnostic utility or causal/therapeutic confirmation. Pathway-restricted screening can recover known biology; proposed drugs remain hypotheses.
evidence.ai_role: Three learned feature-selection methods intersected expression/pathway candidates to construct a disease-specific five-gene panel and evaluate observed tissue-label discrimination.

source_review.scope: Independent publisher full text: data processing, learned hub-gene selection, nomogram evaluation, Results and Discussion; visible date/affiliations. No supplement or new experiment review.
